citations.assessment: Avot 1:3 gives the chain from Shimon the Righteous and the servants maxim. Heilprin quotes only its first clause. The English should preserve Heilprin’s excerpt.
The chapter supplies the story and the gold and silver vessels. It includes multiple generations of teaching. Its narrative and the next commentators’ versions remain separately attributed.
Maimonides distinguishes a gratuity from owed wages and relates how the two pupils misunderstood the maxim. Attribution to Maimonides is secure; his later identification of sects remains his account.
Rashbam explicitly refers to Avot de-Rabbi Natan 5 and discusses the sectarian inheritance dispute.
Heilprin’s reciprocal year entry explicitly attributes its chronology of Tzadok and Boethus to Tzemach David. This is corroboration of the reference, not the external edition itself.
The checked quote reads Ben Antigonus brought the firstborn animals and they were not accepted from him. Keep Heilprin’s wording and signal the witnessed difference.
Heilprin’s Nittai article gives forms for the adjacent firstborn notice, including Ben Attitas and Antinus. It is a cross-reference to the rejected offerings discussion.
The reciprocal article and Yoma 9a establish the high priest reference. The relative dating is Heilprin’s account, also recorded at Almanac 3460:3.
The Mishnah gives Yose rather than Yosef, and says the pair received from them. Heilprin’s entries 1904 and 1905 discuss forms. Preserve the local name forms and qualification of pupils.

holds.reason: The bibliographic expansion is supported by the Almanac’s reciprocal attribution, while the exact dated passage in an edition of Tzemach David remains uncollated.
